research_rationale:
Executive Order 13667 (Blocking Property of Certain Persons Contributing to the Conflict in the Central African Republic; 79 FR 28387) is held in the Federal Register print (FR Doc. 2014-11442) and was read in full. The 30-clause inventory (the opening declaration and sections 1 to 12 with their paragraphs) matches the printed text; the clause numbered sec1-i-8 spans paragraph (A)(8) and paragraphs (B) through (E) of section 1(a)(ii). The print refers to an Annex in sections 1(a)(i) and 9 but contains none (the final PDF page carries only the filing note), so no Annex content is asserted. The order has no sunset or terminating condition of its own. A sentence-by-sentence search of the held texts that print the number 13667 (the Federal Register print, continuation notices, other Federal Register documents and CFR text) for revocation, supersession, rescission, termination, amendment or repeal language next to the number found none. The Federal Register catalog search (later-events:ofr_catalog) returned only cross-references to this order from Central African Republic notices and related orders. The other general instrument in the packet, Executive Order 14294 of May 9, 2025 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations), does not print this number and states a prosecution policy for criminal regulatory offenses, which gives no reason to treat any clause as extinguished. Because the order depends on a declared emergency, the 12 annual continuation notices held for it are attached to every clause; the last, the Notice of May 4, 2026, continues the emergency beyond May 12, 2026, which covers 2026-10-14. Every clause is operative on that date.

The Notice of May 4, 2026 itself acts under section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)) and the emergency rests on IEEPA, so the principal authorities were still operating in 2026; nothing held shows that any authority cited in the order expired or was repealed.","independent_command_check":"The order is a set of continuing commands, prohibitions, findings, definitions, delegations and a reporting authorization. The Annex reference in sections 1(a)(i) and 9 is decided as a command that continues; the held print has no Annex text and the claim does not assert which persons it lists."}
